notes: The analog retro-soul engineering and arranging preset — the Daptone house sound, and the rhythm section that cut half of *Back to Black*. The entry calls the technical doctrine the entry: "a converted two-family house in Bushwick, built with **no computers — no Pro Tools, no digital reverb — tape machines and a CD recorder only**… Practically: few mics, heavy towel damping on the kick and snare, a high-tuned dry snare hit hard on 2&4, closed quiet hats, no 16th carpet, no reverb, single-stroke march fills, and the whole band tracked live in one room so bleed is the reverb." That gives the hardest accent tier in the section against a hat fill density of 0.08, a `quantizeStrength` of 0.58 (no click), and straight single-stroke `snareRoll` figures with almost no gap or descent. **This is the label preset, not the band**: it is written wider than the Sharon Jones & the Dap-Kings model deliberately, because the entry gives the preset a 62–128 span with "the half-time backbeat (snare on 3) as the signature slow option" and a roster beyond one frontwoman — so the kick density, the ghost map and the percussion set are broader here while the doctrine is identical. That overlap is by design; the research describes one sound, and the two models differ in scope rather than in invented detail. Harmony is "minor-mode 2-bar funk vamps (m7, dorian) and major-key `I–IV–V` soul; the horn line supplies the changes, and there is no modulation" — the single-chord vamp and I–IV–V are the two families the entry names. Bass is "flatwound electric bass through a valve amp, muted, locked to the kick in 8ths, cut in the same pass as the drums. Never an 808, never a sub." ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are all drum probabilities and velocity bands and every melody figure; the research documents the studio build, the ban on digital and the *Back to Black* cross-credit, not numbers. ⚠ The half-time slow option is named but not encoded — one model states one placement.
